messages:
jia: Heads-up — I'm proposing an automatic "model variant spill" mechanism: when a primary model (eg redwood-13b-std) is saturated for a tenant/region, route new requests to a cheaper/quantized variant automatically instead of queueing or failing. Wanted early feedback on API surface + console UX + telemetry.

sam: +1 for the idea, we need clear rules about which requests are eligible. user-facing SLOs matter. do we allow this for all routes or opt-in per-route? :thinking:

linda: From PM: opt-in per-route makes the most sense. some customers (financial/legal) won't accept automatic downgrade. Default should be opt-out for enterprise.

mike: Runtime concerns: we can implement capacity-based triggers at the serving layer — e.g. queue length or active-kernel saturation per model variant. But we must avoid thundering migrations of in-flight KV cache size differences.

nina: Telemetry callout: we need histograms for "fallback.rate" by tenant, model, region, and a trace tag showing why a request was spilled (reason=capacity/priority/quota). Also expose total extra-tokens-cost from spill.

sam: API idea: accept an optional header to control behavior: `X-Variant-Fallback: off | best-effort | strict` where best-effort allows spill to a compatible variant; strict = return 429 instead. Also add `X-Preferred-Variants: redwood-13b-q4|redwood-13b-int8` to express order.

jia: example YAML for route config I sketched:```yaml
route: "/generate"
allow_fallback: true
fallback_policy:
  mode: "capacity"
  priority_order:
    - "redwood-13b-q4"
    - "redwood-13b-int8"
  max_latency_penalty_ms: 120
  tenant_overrides:
    premium: { allow: false }
    standard: { allow: true }
```

linda: Nice. UX question: in the console route editor should this be a simple toggle + prioritized list? and show historical fallback % and cost delta?

console-bot: Deploy preview: we can surface a "Fallback health" card per route with: fallback_rate (1h/24h), avg_latency_penalty, cost_delta_estimate, top-tenants-by-fallback (anonymized).

mike: One runtime caveat: variants might have slightly different tokenization or stop behavior. We need compatibility checks when a model is registered as a fallback candidate. Suggest adding a lightweight compatibility test (same tokenizer, response shape, compatible function-calling semantics).

sam: Good point. Add a preflight check step when adding variant to priority list. If incompatible, console should warn and block it.

nina: Alerting thresholds: suggest page when fallback_rate > 5% for > 5m for premium tenants or > 20% for standard. Also send info alert when any tenant sees an unexpected fallback spike (+50% vs baseline).

jia: What about quotas and billing? If we spill to a cheaper quantized variant, do we bill the cheaper token rate automatically? We must be explicit to customers.

linda: Billing: yes, bill based on executed variant unit-cost. We need clear billing docs and console transparency. If a customer pins a variant, then we must not auto-spill.

sam: Implementation approach: (1) annotate model instances with capacity signals (active_rps, free_slots), (2) maintain per-tenant route policy, (3) at routing decision, if primary can't accept within latency_slo, consult ordered variants and attempt spill. Must be fast (<=2ms added decision time).

mike: Also add backoff when spill target is temporarily saturated too — don't oscillate. Maybe exponential backoff per-tenant+route. and circuit-breaker to fall back to queueing/429 when all variants saturated.

jia: UX for rollouts: let teams run a canary where 10% of overflow is spilled to a new variant, with metrics compared to control. That helps validate quality delta.

console-bot: Feature suggestion: in the rollout modal include: canary_percent, min_requests_before_eval, eval_prometheus_query (or use our builtin evaluation harness). Show side-by-side outputs for sampled requests (privacy-preserving).

nina: Telemetry detail: annotate traces with `routing.decision` = primary|spill:variant_name and `routing.reason` = capacity|quota|priority. Also tag `fallback_origin` (auto|manual). This is important for postmortems.

sam: Security note: ensure KMS/tenant isolation preserved across model variants — fallback must not accidentally route data into a variant hosted in a different tenant boundary (esp dedicated vs hosted). Enforce policy at policy-eval time.

linda: Product ask: surface an "accept degraded output" checkbox for routes where fallback is allowed, and an audit log entry whenever auto-spill occurred. Customers can disable auto-spill via enterprise policy.

mike: Quick sketch of API response header: `X-Routed-Variant: redwood-13b-q4; reason=capacity; fallback=true` so customers can instrument. Also add response metric labels for billing pipeline.

jia: We should add a small consent text in quickstart docs and onboarding explaining fallback semantics. Also add a test CLI to simulate saturation locally: `rictl simulate-spill --model redwood-13b-std --target redwood-13b-q4 --rps 500`

sam: Open questions: who owns the feature flag + rollout? eng-platform owns runtime + API, devex owns docs + CLI, product owns policy defaults, eng-sre owns alerts.

linda: Can we ship a minimal v1 with: header control + per-route toggle + telemetry + billing mapping, and keep auto circuit-breakers for later? timeline: 3 sprints?

mike: v1 sounds doable if we limit the preflight compatibility checks to tokenizer+function-calls only. full KV cache tuning later.

nina: I'll add the alert rules and dashboards once we have metric names. propose metrics: `redwood.routing.fallback.count`, `redwood.routing.fallback.latency_penalty_ms`, `redwood.routing.fallback.cost_delta_tokens` with tags model, tenant, route, region.

jia: Thanks. I'll put up a PR with the route schema + API header docs and a console mock. tagging @sam @mike @nina for review. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder: create RFC in the `platform/routing` docs folder and add the design doc link to the PR."
